title.en: The search for genetic material and the RNA world
title.kn: ಆನುವಂಶಿಕ ವಸ್ತುವಿನ ಹುಡುಕಾಟ ಮತ್ತು RNA ಜಗತ್ತು

hook.en: Until the 1940s most scientists thought proteins carried genetic information. A few clever experiments with bacteria and viruses proved them wrong.
hook.kn: 1940ರವರೆಗೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ ವಿಜ್ಞಾನಿಗಳು ಪ್ರೋಟೀನ್ ಆನುವಂಶಿಕ ವಸ್ತು ಎಂದು ಭಾವಿಸಿದ್ದರು. ಬ್ಯಾಕ್ಟೀರಿಯಾ ಮತ್ತು ವೈರಸ್ ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು ಇದನ್ನು ತಪ್ಪೆಂದು ತೋರಿಸಿದವು.

body.en: In 1928 Griffith injected mice with Streptococcus pneumoniae. Live S strain (smooth, capsulated) killed mice; R strain did not; heat-killed S did not; but heat-killed S mixed with live R killed the mice, and live S bacteria were recovered. Some 'transforming principle' had passed from S to R. Avery, MacLeod and McCarty showed it was DNA: only DNase stopped transformation. In 1952 Hershey and Chase grew bacteriophages with radioactive phosphorus (³²P, labels DNA) or sulphur (³⁵S, labels protein). After infection and blending, radioactivity entered bacteria only with ³²P: DNA is the genetic material.
body.kn: ಗ್ರಿಫಿತ್ 1928ರಲ್ಲಿ ಪರಿವರ್ತನೆಯನ್ನು ಕಂಡರು. ಏವರಿ, ಮ್ಯಾಕ್ಲಿಯೋಡ್, ಮೆಕ್‌ಕಾರ್ಟಿ ಅದು DNA ಎಂದು ತೋರಿಸಿದರು. ಹರ್ಷಿ ಮತ್ತು ಚೇಸ್ 1952ರಲ್ಲಿ ³²P ಮತ್ತು ³⁵S ಬಳಸಿ DNA ಆನುವಂಶಿಕ ವಸ್ತು ಎಂದು ಸಾಬೀತುಪಡಿಸಿದರು.

title.en: Board: experiments that found the genetic material

say.en: Griffith injected mice with Streptococcus pneumoniae. Live S killed them; R did not; heat-killed S did not; but heat-killed S with live R killed them.
Avery, MacLeod and McCarty purified the transforming principle: only DNase stopped transformation, so it was DNA.
Hershey and Chase labelled phage DNA with radioactive phosphorus and phage protein with radioactive sulphur, then let them infect bacteria.
After blending, radioactive phosphorus was inside the bacteria, while radioactive sulphur stayed outside: DNA, not protein, enters and carries the genetic information.
Why DNA for storage? RNA's 2-prime OH makes it reactive and quick to mutate, and it can be a catalyst; DNA is more stable. RNA probably came first.

title.en: Griffith and Avery: do the mice die?

narration.en: Only live smooth-strain bacteria kill mice. Decide for each injection whether the mice die or live.

text.en: Heat-killed S strain mixed with live R strain
Heat-killed S extract treated with protease, mixed with live R
Heat-killed S extract treated with RNase, mixed with live R
Heat-killed S extract treated with DNase, mixed with live R

explanation.en: Live S kills; R and heat-killed S do not. Heat-killed S with live R kills, because R is transformed into S. Treating the S extract with protease or RNase still allows transformation, but DNase stops it: the transforming principle is DNA.
explanation.kn: ಜೀವಂತ S ಕೊಲ್ಲುತ್ತದೆ; ಬಿಸಿಯಿಂದ ಕೊಂದ S + ಜೀವಂತ R ಕೂಡ ಕೊಲ್ಲುತ್ತದೆ. DNase ಮಾತ್ರ ರೂಪಾಂತರವನ್ನು ತಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: Properties of genetic material and the RNA world

body.en: A genetic material must replicate, be chemically and structurally stable, allow slow changes (mutation) for evolution, and express itself as Mendelian characters. The 2'-OH group makes RNA reactive and labile, and RNA can act as a catalyst; it mutates faster. DNA is more stable, and thymine instead of uracil adds stability. So RNA was probably the first genetic material, and DNA evolved later for stable storage. RNA is better at expressing characters; DNA depends on RNA for protein synthesis.
body.kn: ಆನುವಂಶಿಕ ವಸ್ತು ಪ್ರತಿಕೃತಿ ಮಾಡಿಕೊಳ್ಳಬೇಕು, ಸ್ಥಿರವಾಗಿರಬೇಕು. RNAಯ 2'-OH ಗುಂಪು ಅದನ್ನು ಅಸ್ಥಿರಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. RNA ಮೊದಲ ಆನುವಂಶಿಕ ವಸ್ತು; ಸ್ಥಿರತೆಗಾಗಿ DNA ನಂತರ ವಿಕಾಸವಾಯಿತು.

problem.en: In the Hershey–Chase experiment, where would you find most radioactivity after blending and centrifuging, for (a) ³⁵S phages, (b) ³²P phages?

steps.en: ³⁵S labels the protein coat, which stays outside the bacterium and is removed by blending; it stays in the supernatant.
³²P labels DNA, which enters the bacterium; the bacteria form the pellet.
So the genetic material that entered was DNA.
